### Describe the Bug Many parts of the codebase assume `PUBLIC_URL` is a full absolute URL (`https://example.com`) but the default is `/`, causing warnings, silent failures, and broken URLs across core features.
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/packages/env/src/constants/defaults.ts#L9-L12]() ### To Reproduce ### API **Issues WARN on every start** when `PUBLIC_URL` is not an absolute URL (i.e. with the default `'/'`):
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/app.ts#L123-L125]() **Admin app URL is relative** and built from `PUBLIC_URL` at startup, produces `'/admin'` instead of
`'https://example.com/admin'`:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/app.ts#L282]() ## OpenAPI Specifications `SpecificationsService` has an **explicit workaround** for the default value but it is insufficient. (see directus/directus#27691)
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/specifications.ts#L96-L97]() I closed directus/directus#27691 because this is a bigger issue than just `@directus/specs` but just in case the research no the Spec becomes relevant you can expand to see research details.
OAS Specification Notes Researching further against the OAS 3.0.1 Specifications: [4.7.1.1 Fixed Fields]() | Field Name | Type | Description | | -- | -- | -- | | servers | [Server Object]() | An array of Server Objects, which provide connectivity information to a target server. If the servers property is not provided, or is an empty array, the default value would be a Server Object with a url value of `/`. | Suggests to me that `/` would be a valid URL. This, however, doesn't match the Directus use case, since then the host for the OAS Spec Interpreter (e.g. Swagger-Editor) would be at the same domain as Directus and there would be conflicts. In cases where the @directus/specs package is used to generate a static file to then feed into another system, it would work... but that defeats the purpose of the dynamic builder and conflicts with the description "This is a dynamically generated API..." [4.7.5.1 Server Object]() | Field Name | Type | Description | | -- | -- | -- | | url | string | REQUIRED. A URL to the target host. This URL supports Server Variables and MAY be relative, to indicate that the host location is relative to the location where the OpenAPI document is being served. Variable substitutions will be made when a variable is named in `{`brackets`}`. | | description | string | An optional string describing the host designated by the URL. [CommonMark]() syntax MAY be used for rich text representation. | | variables | Map< />string, Server Variable Object< /> | A map between a variable name and its value. The value is used for substitution in the server’s URL template. | The current implementation does not support multiple servers and building that out would be an edge case with limited (if any) users. It may be useful to implement the `PUBLIC_URL` based on a different ternary (currently `isDefaultPublicUrl`). If so, `isPublicUrlRelativePath` would make sense and catch the default case of `/`: ```diff - const isDefaultPublicUrl = env['PUBLIC_URL'] === '/'; + const isPublicUrlRelativePath = (env['PUBLIC_URL'] as string).startsWith('/'); - const url = isDefaultPublicUrl && host ? host : (env['PUBLIC_URL'] as string); + const rawUrl = isPublicRelativePath && host ? host : (env['PUBLIC_URL'] as string); + // Ensure the URL is absolute so OAS clients can resolve it + const url = rawUrl && !rawUrl.startsWith('http') ? `http://${rawUrl}` : rawUrl; // ... const spec: OpenAPIObject = { openapi: '3.0.1', info: { title: 'Dynamic API Specification', description: 'This is a dynamically generated API specification for all endpoints existing on the current project.', version: hashedVersion, }, servers: [ { url, description: 'Your current Directus instance.', }, ], ```
## TUS File Uploads **Generated upload URLs become relative paths** (e.g. `'/files/tus/'`) and the `relativeLocation` flag inverts making it `true` only when `PUBLIC_URL` starts with `http`, so with `'/'` the server sends absolute `Location` headers pointing at relative paths:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/tus/server.ts#L134-L139]() ## Email Notifications All email notifications build their links from `PUBLIC_URL`. With the default `'/'`, every link in every outbound email is a relative path, making them non-functional. **User invite link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/users.ts#L163-L165]() **Email verification link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/users.ts#L547-L552]() **Password reset link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/users.ts#L624-L626]() **Share notification link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/shares.ts#L164]() **Comment mention link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/comments.ts#L134-L138]() **Notification manage-account link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/notifications.ts#L37-L40]() **Import/export result link:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/import-export.ts#L790]() **Project logo URL in email template:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/mail/index.ts#L142-L147]() ## OAuth / SSO All OAuth callback and redirect URLs are built from `PUBLIC_URL`. With `'/'`, OAuth provider registration breaks, and redirect validation throws at runtime. **Callback URL generation** falls back to `PUBLIC_URL` when no `AUTH_ALLOWED_PUBLIC_URLS` match; `'/'` produces an invalid callback registered with the OAuth provider:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/auth/utils/generate-callback-url.ts#L39-L47]() **Login redirect validation throws at runtime** if `PUBLIC_URL` is not parseable as an absolute URL:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/auth/utils/resolve-login-redirect.ts#L63-L70]() **OpenID error redirect to admin login:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/auth/drivers/openid.ts#L484-L488]() **OpenID post-login redirect:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/auth/drivers/openid.ts#L521-L522]() **OpenID TFA setup redirect:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/auth/drivers/openid.ts#L589]() **OAuth2 TFA setup redirect:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/auth/drivers/oauth2.ts#L493]() ## MCP **Canonical resource/metadata URLs lose their host** because `'/'` has its trailing slash stripped, leaving an empty base, so `resourceUrl` becomes `'/mcp'` and `metadataUrl` becomes `'/.well-known/...'` which is unusable for external MCP clients:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/ai/mcp/utils.ts#L9-L16]() **MCP OAuth** `new URL()` **throws on relative input**, returning a 403 to the client:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/controllers/mcp/oauth.ts#L122-L125]() **MCP OAuth login URL:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/controllers/mcp/oauth.ts#L359]() **MCP OAuth consent decision URL:**
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/controllers/mcp/oauth.ts#L415]() ## License Manager My guess is that this is where you'll first start to see this bug manifest in a material way to your core business since you'll be receiving `public_url: '/'` to the licensing service on every license check:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/license/manager.ts#L289-L291]() ## Extensions Extension dependency asset URLs become relative paths, which may break cross-origin extension setups:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/extensions/lib/get-shared-deps-mapping.ts#L25]() ## Telemetry Reports `url: '/'` to the telemetry service the instance. I wonder what the internal telemetry looks like here... could be an early indication of the issue with license manager.
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/telemetry/lib/get-report.ts#L60]() ## Deployment Webhooks Sends `'/'` as the instance public URL when registering deployment webhooks:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/deployment.ts#L287-L288]() ## Server Info Uses `PUBLIC_URL` as the server's `serviceId` in health checks:
[https://github.com/directus/directus/blob/33ec9381437e768aad2dfe5cdae8c3c1fc85e2ae/api/src/services/server.ts#L224]() ### Directus Version v12 ### Hosting Strategy Self-Hosted (Docker Image) ### Database n/a

## Background During the audit performed for PR directus/directus#27316, a significant number of gaps were found between the `@directus/specs` package and the actual REST API surface of `@directus/api`. This issue is being created to better manage the process of addressing what gaps were discovered and make it easier to chunk the changes. This issue catalogs every gap found so far. It may not be exhaustive of every possible spec issue, but it covers all cases identified during a systematic review of the controller routes against the spec paths in `packages/specs/src/paths/`. I hope this catches the project up to a manageable state for future contributions. Related: directus/directus#20972, directus/directus#26539, directus/directus#25179 --- ## Currently Undocumented Paths ### Always On - [ ] **Document** `/dashboards` **and** `/panels` directus/directus#27701 Both manage Insights records (`directus_dashboards`, `directus_panels`) and follow the same shape. Bundling them in one PR is reasonable. Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}` for each. Source: `api/src/controllers/dashboards.ts`, `api/src/controllers/panels.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/notifications` **and** `/translations` directus/directus#27764 Manages in-app notification records (`directus_notifications`). Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/notifications.ts`.
Manages custom translation records (`directus_translations`). Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/translations.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/deployments` directus/directus#27767 Provider-scoped deployment management. Routes: GET `/deployments`, GET/PATCH/DELETE `/deployments/{provider}`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/projects`, GET/PATCH `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}/runs`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}/runs/stats`, POST `/deployments/{provider}/projects/{id}/deploy`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/runs/{id}`, POST `/deployments/{provider}/runs/{id}/cancel`, GET `/deployments/{provider}/dashboard`. Source: `api/src/controllers/deployment.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/shares` directus/directus#27763 Manages content share records (`directus_shares`). Includes three special-purpose endpoints beyond the standard CRUD set. Routes: GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, PATCH, PATCH `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`, POST `/shares/auth` (no user credential required, accepts optional password), POST `/shares/invite` (send email invitations), GET `/shares/info/{id}` (public endpoint, no authentication required, validates expiry and usage limits). Source: `api/src/controllers/shares.ts`. - [ ] **Document** `/extensions/registry`, `/extensions/registry/account/{pk}`, `/extensions/registry/extension/{pk}`, `/extensions/registry/install`, `/extensions/registry/reinstall`, `/extensions/registry/uninstall/{pk}`, `/extensions/{pk}` (DELETE), and `/extensions/sources/{chunk}` Only `GET /extensions`, `PATCH /extensions/{name}`, and `PATCH /extensions/{bundle}/{name}` are currently documented (`packages/specs/src/paths/extensions/`). The registry browse/install/uninstall routes and the `DELETE /extensions/{pk}` / `GET /extensions/sources/{chunk}` routes have no spec coverage at all. Source: `api/src/controllers/extensions.ts`. ### ENV Gated - [ ] **Document ENV-gated subsystems:** `/files/tus`**,** `/mcp`**,** `/mcp-oauth/clients` directus/directus#27766 Use the same env-gating pattern introduced for `/metrics` in PR directus/directus#27316. `/files/tus` (requires `TUS_ENABLED=true`): POST `/files/tus`, HEAD `/files/tus/{id}`, OPTIONS `/files/tus/{id}`, PATCH `/files/tus/{id}`, DELETE `/files/tus/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/tus.ts`. `/mcp` (requires `mcp_enabled` system setting): GET `/mcp`, POST `/mcp`. Source: `api/src/controllers/mcp/index.ts`. `/mcp-oauth/clients` (requires `MCP_OAUTH_ENABLED=true`): GET, POST, GET `/{id}`, DELETE, DELETE `/{id}`. Source: `api/src/controllers/mcp/oauth-clients.ts`. ## Paths with incorrect documentation - [ ] **Add missing methods to** `/server`**,** `/files`**, and** `/flows` directus/directus#27765 `/server`: GET `/server/health` (200 or 503, requires `HEALTHCHECK_ENABLED != false`) `/files`: POST `/files/import` (import file from remote URL, accepts `url`, optional `data` and `filterMimeType`). `/flows`: GET `/flows/trigger/{id}` and POST `/flows/trigger/{id}`. - [X] **Add missing methods to** `/users` [directus/directus#27761]() `/users`: POST `/users/register` (public self-registration, rate-limited, accepts `email`, `password`, optional `first_name`, `last_name`, `verification_url`), GET `/users/register/verify-email` (email verification redirect), POST `/users/me/tfa/generate` (returns secret and QR code URI), POST `/users/me/tfa/enable` (requires `secret` and `otp`). Note: `/users/me/tfa/disable` and `/users/{id}/tfa/disable` are already documented. - [X] **Remove incorrect query parameters from** `/collections` **and** `/fields` directus/directus#27762 Confirmed by @ComfortablyCoding during review of PR directus/directus#27316 with references to the relevant controller lines. GET `/collections`: remove `Offset` and `Meta` (API accepts no query parameters on this endpoint). GET `/fields`: remove `Limit`, `Page`, and `Sort` (API accepts no query parameters on this endpoint). GET `/fields/{collection}`: remove `Sort` (API accepts no query parameters on this endpoint). - [ ] **Add SEARCH method to all affected endpoints** directus/directus#27760 The API implements the SEARCH HTTP method as an alternative to GET for complex filtered queries. It is not documented on any endpoint. Affected paths (at minimum): `/collections`, `/comments`, `/dashboards`, `/files`, `/folders`, `/items/{collection}`, `/notifications`, `/operations`, `/panels`, `/permissions`, `/presets`, `/revisions`, `/roles`, `/shares`, `/translations`, `/users`, `/versions`. ## Validation warnings When loading the generated OAS from `GET /server/specs/oas` without an authentication token, two pre-existing validation warnings appear for the `Query` and `x-metadata` schema references. They do not appear when the spec is generated with an authenticated token. These are not introduced by any of the changes in PR directus/directus#27316 and may resolve as spec coverage catches up. ## Known exclusions `/license` is intentionally not exposed in the public spec (confirmed as internal use only by @ComfortablyCoding during review of PR directus/directus#27316). `/ai/chat`, `/ai/object`, and `/ai/files` (all under the `AI_ENABLED=true` gate) are intentionally not exposed in the public spec. All three check `req.accountability?.app` and reject non-studio sessions with a 403. They are studio-internal tooling, not a public API surface. Confirmed by PR descriptions: [#26259]() ("intended for in-studio use only"), [#26862]() ("requires `app: true` accountability"), [#26722]() (server-side proxy for the studio file-attachment feature). ### Describe the Bug

The Anthropic AI assistant raises `Tool reference '<tool-name>-<uid>' not found in available tools` after the user navigates between content items or interacts with any UI surface that remounts a `v-form` (drawer-batch, comparison modal, overlay item content, HMR in dev). The error comes from Anthropic's API backend, not the AI SDK.

The error is currently latent on `main` and is surfaced by aggressive prompt caching (in-progress on `bry/ai-prompt-caching`) but the root cause exists today.

### Root cause

The form-aware tools are registered per `v-form` component instance with `componentUid` baked into their names (`app/src/components/v-form/composables/use-ai-tools.ts:26,47`):

```ts
defineTool({
  name: `read-form-values-${componentUid}`,
  ...
});
defineTool({
  name: `set-form-values-${componentUid}`,
  ...
});
```

`api/src/ai/providers/anthropic-tool-search.ts` marks every tool `deferLoading: true` and adds the `toolSearchBm25_20251119` virtual tool. With deferred loading, Anthropic returns `tool_reference` blocks that name actual tools (e.g. `read-form-values-878`). Anthropic resolves those names against the **current** request's tools array on every turn.

When the v-form unmounts (page nav, modal open/close, HMR) `componentUid` rotates. Conversation history still references the old name, and any cached Anthropic state for our prefix references the old name too. Current tools array has `read-form-values-912`. Resolution fails → 400 from Anthropic, which the UI surfaces as `Tool reference '...' not found in available tools`.

### To Reproduce

1. Enable Anthropic provider, pick a non-Haiku Claude model (Sonnet/Opus — tool-search is skipped on Haiku).
2. Open the AI Assistant on a content item (collection A).
3. Ask: "what's currently in this form?" → AI calls `read-form-values-<uid>` once, answers.
4. Navigate to a different content item (preferably a different collection).
5. Ask another question that hits form tools, e.g. "what's the title here?"
6. Expected: succeeds.
7. Actual: error \"Tool reference 'read-form-values-<oldUid>' not found in available tools\".

Easier to reproduce with prompt caching enabled, but reproducible without.

### Possible fixes

1. **Stabilize the form-tool names** — drop the `componentUid` suffix; add single-active-form policy to `useAiToolsStore` (`app/src/ai/stores/use-ai-tools.ts`) so concurrent v-form mounts (drawer-batch, comparison-modal, overlay-item-content) don't clobber each other. Names become static `read-form-values` / `set-form-values`. Bonus: stabilizes the tools section in the Anthropic cache prefix, which improves cache hit rates.
2. **Bypass Anthropic tool-search** as a stop-gap — return tools as-is from `applyAnthropicToolSearch` (no deferred loading, no `toolSearch`). Eliminates `tool_reference` resolution entirely. Costs more input tokens per request, but caching of tools+system still works.
3. **Wait for the planned 3-tool meta-tool refactor (search / get / execute)** — replaces both the form-aware tools and the Anthropic tool-search dependency, removing this failure mode.

### Directus Version

Confirmed on `bry/ai-prompt-caching` against `directus-version-12`. Latent on main since the tool-search integration shipped (PR #26864).

### Hosting Strategy

Local dev

### Describe the Bug

Field‑conditions that reference other fields via dynamic values such as `{{ b }}` do **not trigger** any UI behavior (visibility, required state, disabled state, etc.), even when the underlying condition is logically true. The issue is not limited to the “required” flag; it affects all condition types (show/hide, disable, and any field‑state logic). 

The same condition works correctly when the dynamic value is replaced with a static literal (e.g., a fixed string or number), which confirms that the condition engine itself is working but that dynamic‑field references are not being resolved inside field‑condition filters. 



### To Reproduce

1. Create a collection with three fields:  
   - Field `a` (any scalar/text type).  
   - Field `b` (same type as `a`).  
   - Field `C` (any type).
2. Open **Settings → Data Model → [your collection]** and edit field `C`. 
3. Set up a condition such as:  
   - Field: `a`  
   - Operator: `equal`  
   - Value: `{{ b }}`  
4. Then choose **any** behavior for `C` when this condition is true, for example:  
   - Show / hide `C`  
   - Disable `C`  
   - Mark `C` as required  
   - Any other UI‑state tied to the condition.
5. Create a new item and set both `a` and `b` to the same value.  
6. Observe that **none** of the configured behaviors for field `C` are applied.  

### Verification:
- Edit the same condition and replace `{{ b }}` with a static literal (e.g., `"same_value"`).  
- Create a new item where `a` equals that literal.  
- All configured behaviors (show/hide, required, disable, etc.) now work correctly, proving that the problem is specifically the dynamic‑value resolution in field‑conditions.

v11.17.4

## Title

Directus 11.12: `/fields/<collection>` remains 403 FORBIDDEN for an admin-policy token after `directus_collections` row repair, cache flush, and full app restart — collection unrecoverable from outside the application

## Body

### TL;DR

On Directus `11.12.0` ([Fly.io](<http://Fly.io>) single-region deploy backed by Supabase Postgres), one specific `content.*` collection is in a state where the permission resolver returns `403 FORBIDDEN` on every `/fields/<collection>`, `/items/<collection>`, and admin UI **field save** call — *even with the Schema Bot user holding a fully-attached Administrator policy (*`admin_access: true`). Every documented recovery path from Issues directus/directus#25760 and [#24411](<https://github.com/directus/directus/issues/24411>) (maintainer-endorsed direct-SQL repair, cache flush, full app restart, `directus_fields` row repopulation) has been attempted and verified to fail. The same token returns `HTTP 200` on `/fields/<sibling-collection>` in the same instance. The stuck row sits indefinitely behind a `--skip-collections` operator workaround on our deploy pipeline.

### Environment

* Directus: `11.12.0`
* Database: PostgreSQL 15 (Supabase managed), accessed via Supavisor transaction pooler.
* Hosting: [Fly.io](<http://Fly.io>) (2-machine deployment); single internal Redis container is not in use; Directus's default in-process cache only.
* Authentication: static token attached to a user whose role has one policy with `admin_access: true` (verified live via `/users/me?fields=policies.policy.admin_access`).

### Symptom

The collection in question (`content.system_messages`) exhibits exactly this pattern:

<!-- linear:table-colwidths:266,266,266 -->
| Endpoint | Other content.\* collections | This collection |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /collections/<name>` | 200, meta populated | 200, meta populated (after repair) |
| `GET /fields/<name>` | 200 | **403 FORBIDDEN** |
| `GET /items/<name>` | 200 | **403 FORBIDDEN** |
| Admin UI → Data Model → field save | succeeds | **403 FORBIDDEN at save** |
| `GET /permissions/me?filter[collection][_eq]=<name>` | enumerated | **missing from enumeration**, despite `admin_access: true` |

The same token, run against any other `content.*` collection (e.g. `coach_schedule`, `sounds`), returns `200`. The issue is per-collection, not per-token.

### What we tried (none worked)

Sequence executed operator-side on 2026-05-12 against the live `cmsdev` dev instance, in order, with verification between each step:

 1. **Defensive backup** of the underlying PG table via `\copy` (procedure never touches `content.*`; backup is paranoia).
 2. **Confirmed clean ghost state**: `SELECT count(*) FROM directus.directus_collections WHERE collection='system_messages';` → 0 (after deleting a prior partial-recovery residue row).
 3. **Single-row INSERT** per Issue directus/directus#25760's maintainer-endorsed workaround:

    ```sql
    INSERT INTO directus.directus_collections (collection) VALUES ('system_messages');
    ```

    `directus_collections` row count → 1. `GET /collections/system_messages` → 200 with non-null `meta` (registered).
 4. **Cache flush**: `POST /utils/cache/clear` → HTTP 200.
 5. Re-test `GET /fields/system_messages` → **HTTP 403**.
 6. **Fly app restart** (both machines healthy after restart, fresh process).
 7. Re-test `GET /fields/system_messages` → **HTTP 403**.
 8. **Hypothesis: collections with zero** `directus_fields` rows might be filtered out of the permission resolver's enumeration. Verified that `coach_schedule` (200 OK) has 6 `directus_fields` rows; `system_messages` (403) had 0. Inserted 5 minimal `directus_fields` rows (one per PG column: `key`, `locale`, `body`, `created_at`, `updated_at`), all default-shape.
 9. **Cache flush** → HTTP 200.
10. **Fly app restart** (second).
11. Re-test `GET /fields/system_messages` → **HTTP 403 still**.
12. **Full rollback**: `DELETE FROM directus.directus_fields WHERE collection='system_messages';` (5 rows) + `DELETE FROM directus.directus_collections WHERE collection='system_messages';` (1 row). Returned to clean ghost state. `content.system_messages` PG table (4 seeded rows) untouched throughout — verified by row count + post-rollback comparison to pre-experiment `\copy` backup.

Earlier (pre-2026-05-12) we also confirmed:

* `directus_permissions` has **0 rows** for `system_messages` (no explicit deny rule — admin policy should bypass `directus_permissions` checks entirely anyway).
* `DELETE /collections/<name>?keep_table=true` returns HTTP 500 with `drop table "<name>" - must be owner of table` — Directus 11.12 attempts `DROP TABLE` despite `keep_table=true` (matches Issue [#24411](<https://github.com/directus/directus/issues/24411>)). Our PG role permissions correctly refuse the drop; if we had transferred ownership we would have lost the 4 seeded rows of editorial content.

### Hypothesis

Directus 11.12's permission resolver has a state we have not identified that prevents this specific collection from being enumerated in admin-policy access lookups. The state appears to be:

* **Not in any of**: `directus_collections.<row>` meta, `directus_fields.<rows>` presence, `directus_permissions.<rows>`, the static token's policy attachment, the in-process schema cache, or any state cleared by a full container restart.
* **Possibly in**: a code path keyed on the *originating creation context* of the `directus_collections` row (the row was first created mid-2026-05-06 via a half-completed admin-UI "Make Collection Visible" flow after a Postgres migration created the underlying table); or in a state initialised at policy/role assignment time that survives subsequent row recreation.

We don't have visibility into the resolver's internal state. The Schema Bot is a service account; we cannot easily re-impersonate a "fresh" admin context to probe.

### Workaround currently in place

Our deploy pipeline's reconcile script ([reconcile-directus-content.ts](<https://github.com/Tinnitus-App/naluma-app/blob/main/tools/directus-schema/reconcile-directus-content.ts>), which auto-recovers `content.*` schema drift via atomic `POST /collections` with embedded `fields:[]`) has been carrying a `--skip-collections=system_messages` flag for the single stuck collection. This prevents the apply-schema step from failing on every push to `main`, at the cost of leaving that one row unmanageable through Directus. Editorial content edits to its 4 production rows go through direct SQL until this is resolved.

### What would help

1. **Confirmation** that the symptom matches a known internal state in 11.x — even "this happens when X" without a fix narrows the scope.
2. **Diagnostic queries** we can run against the Postgres tables to identify *which* state is the lock keying off — e.g. is there a `directus_*` table or column we haven't inspected that holds enumeration-eligibility flags?
3. **A version since-when this is fixed** — we can run a controlled bump if you confirm a later 11.x or 12.x resolves it.
4. **A force-reset path** — e.g. an admin SQL recipe that drops the relevant resolver state for a single collection without touching the underlying PG table or `content.*` data.

We have the original migration SQL that created the table, the backup CSV of its 4 seeded rows, full audit and ADR documentation of every recovery attempt, and an authenticated Schema Bot token with Administrator policy. Happy to run additional diagnostics on the live instance and report back.

### References

* Directus Issue directus/directus#25760 — `directus_collections` row workaround for `apply` mode (we followed this and it didn't help on the deeper case here).
* Directus Issue [#24411](<https://github.com/directus/directus/issues/24411>) — `keep_table=true` ignored on `DELETE /collections`. Closed not-planned. Maintainer recommendation we attempted was: "Manually manage metadata cleanup by directly removing entries from directus_collections and directus_fields tables, bypassing the Directus UI."
* We have an internal audit and ADR documenting the full investigation, recovery attempt, and rollback procedure. Available on request — happy to share with a maintainer if it helps diagnosis.

### Reproduction context (best-effort)

We cannot offer a clean repro recipe because the bug appears to require a specific historical path (half-completed "Make Visible" → partial `directus_collections` row state → fresh row recreation later that doesn't shake the lock). If a maintainer has time to look at the *symptoms* live on our dev instance, we can provide read-only access to a debugging session — separate from this report.

I realize I'm not using the latest version of Directus in this bug report, but I have tested the bug locally in the latest version of Directus.

When querying a versioned (version: "draft") item that contains an M2A field, GraphQL fails with:
`Cannot return null for non-nullable field pages_blocks.id`

This happens because one of the M2A junction rows is returned as null in the draft version, even though the block exists and is valid in the Admin UI.

4. Add an M2A field "blocks" to page collection and configure to allow faq_blocks.
6. Create an empty page.
7. Create a draft version of the page.
8. In the draft, add a new faq_blocks and save the draft version.
9. Query the page via GraphQL:
```graphql
query {  
  pages_by_id(id: "<page-id>", version: "draft") {
    id
    blocks {
      id
      collection
    }
  }
}
```

GraphQL should return all blocks, including draft changes, without errors.

**Actual Behavior**
```json
{
  "data": {
    "pages_by_id": {
      "id": "...",
      "blocks": [

    }
  ]
}
```

### Describe the Bug

When using custom date formatting in a Datetime field, the W token (week of month) is not supported, even though Directus references the Unicode Date Field Symbol Table.

Additionally, when both Interface and Display are set to Custom Format, using the W token results in an unexpected error message in the UI instead of rendering a value.

According to the Unicode TR35 specification:

w = week of year  (works correctly in Directus)
W = week of month (not working in Directus)

This leads to inconsistent behavior where some valid Unicode tokens are supported while others are ignored or result in an "Unexpected error" message when rendering the field.

### To Reproduce

- Create a collection with a Datetime field
- Set the field Interface to Custom Format
- Set the field Display to Custom Format

- Use the following format:

`'week' W 'of' MMM`

- Save and view the field value

## Expected Behavior

The W token should return the week number within the month, as defined in Unicode TR35.

Example: week 4 of Apr

**Actual Behavior**

- The W token is ignored or produces incorrect output
- In some cases, it throws an unexpected error while rendering

**Working Comparison**

The w token (week of year) works correctly:

`'week' w 'of' Y`

Example output: week 17 of 2026

**Additional Context**
Reference:
https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr35/tr35-dates.html#Date_Field_Symbol_Table

### Directus Version

11.17.3

## Summary

When creating indexes through `directus schema apply`, index creation always runs inside a transaction, which prevents the use of concurrent/online index creation mechanisms (e.g., `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` on PostgreSQL). This can cause table-level locks on large tables, leading to downtime during schema migrations.

## Current Behavior

`applyDiff` (`api/src/utils/apply-diff.ts`) wraps all operations in a single transaction:

```typescript
await transaction(database, async (trx) => {
    let fieldsService = new FieldsService({ knex: trx, schema: ... });
    await fieldsService.createField(collection, ..., mutationOptions);
    // ...
});
```

Since `attemptConcurrentIndex` is never passed, indexes are created via knex's `column.index()` inside the transaction.

Even if `attemptConcurrentIndex` were passed, the `FieldsService` would use the outer transaction's `trx` for `knex.raw('CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ...')`, which would fail on PostgreSQL (concurrent index creation cannot run inside a transaction).

## Existing Infrastructure

The REST API already supports concurrent index creation via the `?concurrentIndexCreation` query parameter. `FieldsService.createField` already implements a two-phase approach:

1. **Inside transaction**: Schema changes (column creation) — index creation is skipped when `attemptConcurrentIndex` is `true`
2. **Outside transaction**: Concurrent index creation via `knex.raw()` with DB-specific syntax

Per-dialect implementations already exist:

| Database | Method |
|----------|--------|
| PostgreSQL | `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` |
| MySQL | `ALGORITHM=INPLACE LOCK=NONE` (with fallback) |
| CockroachDB | `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` |
| Oracle | `CREATE INDEX ... ONLINE` |
| MS SQL | `WITH (ONLINE = ON)` (Enterprise Edition only) |
| SQLite | Not supported |

## Proposed Solution

Adopt the same two-phase approach in `applyDiff`:

1. Run all schema changes inside the transaction (skip index creation)
2. Collect pending index operations during the transaction
3. After the transaction commits, create indexes concurrently outside the transaction

This could be controlled by a CLI flag, e.g., `directus schema apply --concurrent-index-creation`.

## Considerations

- Concurrent index creation failure can leave invalid indexes that need manual cleanup
- Since the index creation happens outside the transaction, it won't be rolled back if it fails
- An opt-in flag may be safer than making it the default behavior

### Describe the Bug

Context

While removing as any assertions in app/src/composables/use-collab.ts, we discovered that the SDK client isn't receiving

the schema generic it needs for proper type inference.

How SDK Generics Work

The Directus SDK is designed around a Schema generic that flows through the entire type system:

// The SDK client accepts a Schema generic                                                                                    
DirectusClient<Schema>                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
// Which propagates to queries                                                                                                
readUsers<Schema, Query>()                                                                                                    
                                                                                                                              
// Which determines what fields are valid                                                                                     
Query<Schema, Item>.fields → QueryFields<Schema, Item>                                                                        
                                                                                                                              
When you provide a proper Schema, the SDK can:                                                                                
1. Know which collections exist (directus_users, directus_files, etc.)                                                        
2. Know field types for each collection                                                                                       
3. Detect relational fields by checking if a field's type exists in the Schema                                                
4. Allow nested object syntax for those relational fields: { avatar: ['id', 'modified_on'] }                                  
                                                                                                                                           

The Problem

The app passes unknown as the Schema generic:

// app/src/sdk.ts
export type SdkClient = DirectusClient<unknown> & AuthenticationClient<unknown> & RestClient<unknown>;

With unknown, the SDK's type inference chain breaks:

 // SDK internals (simplified)                                                                                                 
  type RelationalFields<Schema, Item> = {                                                                                       
    [Key in keyof Item]: Extract<Item[Key], ItemType<Schema>> extends never ? never : Key;                                      
  }[keyof Item];  

type ItemType<Schema> = Schema[keyof Schema];  // With unknown → never     

ItemType<unknown> = unknown[keyof unknown] = unknown[never] = never

RelationalFields<unknown, User> = never (no fields match never)

Object syntax { avatar: [...] } is excluded from valid field types


This forces us to use as any:

fields: ['id', 'first_name', 'last_name', { avatar: ['id', 'modified_on'] }] as any


Possible solution

The SDK exports `CoreSchema` - a pre-defined generic that describes all system collections:

User extends the CoreSchema with the expected data structure hierarchy.

- Query the SDK with a nested field 
- Run vue-tsc

## Summary

Directus schema operations (creating collections, adding fields, modifying tables) remain slow with CockroachDB after introspection optimizations, and field modifications fail due to transaction handling issues.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Issue 1: Transaction Handling Conflicts

CockroachDB handles schema changes differently than PostgreSQL. Schema modifications create **online schema change jobs** that run asynchronously and may perform backfills while the cluster continues serving traffic.

**Key constraints from CockroachDB documentation**:
- Schema changes should **not** be wrapped in explicit multi-statement transactions
- Best practice: **one schema-change operation per transaction**
- Multiple `ALTER TABLE` subcommands should be **combined into a single statement** rather than executed as separate statements

**Reference**: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/online-schema-changes

### Issue 2: Hidden Table Rewrites

Some schema changes trigger table-wide backfills even when not obviously expected:
- Adding columns with defaults
- Computed columns
- Constraint additions/modifications
- TTL-related changes

These operations cause delays as CockroachDB rewrites affected rows across the cluster.

**Reference**: https://www.cockroachlabs.com/docs/stable/row-level-ttl

## Proposed Solutions

### Option 1: Avoid Multi-Statement Schema Transactions

Audit schema operation code paths to ensure schema changes are not wrapped in explicit multi-statement transactions. Where multiple schema changes are currently executed within a single transaction, either:

- Combine them into a single ALTER TABLE statement with multiple subcommands
- Execute them as separate auto-committed statements outside of an explicit transaction

### Option 2: CockroachDB-Specific Schema Change Handling
Add conditional logic for CockroachDB that:

- Batches compatible alterations into single statements
- Executes schema changes outside explicit transactions
- Adds retry logic to handle schema change job conflicts

## Additional Context

### What's Been Fixed
- CockroachDB-specific introspection using `crdb_internal.*` tables instead of `pg_catalog.*` virtual views

### What Still Needs Work
1. Audit transaction boundaries around schema operations
2. Refactor to avoid multi-statement schema transactions
3. Combine ALTER TABLE subcommands where possible
4. Investigate which field types/defaults trigger hidden rewrites

### To Reproduce

1. **Setup CockroachDB cluster** with SSL certificates
2. **Configure Directus** with `DB_CLIENT: cockroachdb`
3. **Create database** with existing 20+ tables
4. **Create fields** this request should be taking longer the more fields you have
5. **Observe** The creation of fields taking longer the more fields exist
6. **Update a field** attempt to modify a field on an existing collection
7. **Observe**: Operation fails with transaction error

## Summary

Add hierarchical organization support for Flows, matching the existing Collections folder/grouping behavior. This allows users to organize flows into folders, nest flows under other flows, and reorder via drag-and-drop.

## Problem

As projects grow, users accumulate many flows serving different purposes (webhooks, scheduled tasks, event handlers, utilities). Currently, flows display in a flat alphabetical list with no way to organize or group them. Collections already support folders and nesting, but Flows lack this capability.

## Solution

### New Capabilities
- **Folders**: Create organizational folders (`trigger: null`) to group related flows
- **Nesting**: Nest flows under folders OR other flows (e.g., group utility flows under the main flow they support)
- **Drag-and-drop**: Reorder flows and move them between groups
- **Persistent collapse**: Expand/collapse state saved per-user in localStorage
- **Search**: Filter flows by name, status, description, or trigger type (parents remain visible when children match)

### Database Changes
New columns on `directus_flows`:
- `group` (UUID, nullable) - References parent flow/folder
- `sort` (integer, nullable) - Sort order within group  
- `collapse` (string, default 'open') - Collapse state: 'open', 'closed', 'locked'

### Shared Infrastructure
Extracted reusable components/composables that can be used for other grouped lists:
- `use-expand-collapse.ts` - Generic expand/collapse with localStorage
- `use-visibility-tree.ts` - Search visibility with parent propagation
- `flatten-grouped-items.ts` - Hierarchical flattening utility
- `grouped-list/` components - Recursive tree item, dialog, context menu

### Additional Enhancements
- Collections search now also matches on field names
- Documentation updated for both Flows and Collections organization
- AI tools prompts updated with organization guidance

## Migration

The migration:
1. Adds `sort`, `group`, `collapse` columns to `directus_flows`
2. Initializes `sort` values alphabetically for existing flows (preserves current ordering)

Tested on database with 27 flows and 107 collections.

## Related

- Follows existing Collections folder/grouping pattern
- Extends `directus_flows` schema with self-referential relation

### Describe the Bug

We are experiencing an issue with LDAP user role assignment in Directus.

We have an LDAP configuration where first-time LDAP logins automatically create a Directus user and assign a default role: Restricted. This part works as expected.

However, after an admin (or another authorized user) manually changes the role of that LDAP-created user to a different role, the user’s role later reverts back to Restricted automatically without any manual action. This effectively overrides the admin’s explicit role assignment.

This behavior suggests that the default role assignment for LDAP users might be re-applied after initial provisioning (possibly on subsequent logins or via a background sync), which results in unintended role downgrades.

Impact: Users who were granted elevated permissions temporarily lose access and are forced back to the restricted permission set.

### To Reproduce

Configure LDAP authentication in Directus.

Configure/enable a default role for LDAP users, set to Restricted.

Log in with an LDAP user who does not yet exist in Directus.

A new Directus user is created automatically.

The user is assigned the Restricted role.

Log in as an admin.

Open the newly created user in User Management.

Change the user’s role from Restricted to another role (e.g., Editor/Custom Role) and save.

Wait for some time and/or have the user log in again.

Observe that the user’s role is automatically changed back to Restricted.

Actual Result: The role reverts to Restricted automatically after being manually changed by an admin.
Expected Result: The default LDAP role should only be applied on first-time provisioning (user creation). After that, an admin’s manual role change should persist and not be overwritten.

### Directus Version

v11.12.0

### Hosting Strategy

Self-Hosted (Docker Image)

### Database

pgsql16
